title: Quasiparticle-resolved variational theory of Andreev spin qubits
abstract: An Andreev spin qubit stores a single unpaired spin, yet its coupling to the superconducting phase can be dominated by coherent virtual quasiparticle pairs. We develop a continuum variational description of the odd-parity doublet in a quantum-dot Josephson junction with Coulomb interaction and spin-dependent background tunneling. Retaining configurations with up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles provides compact analytical expressions for energies and wavefunctions. We benchmark the results against numerical renormalization group calculations and identify sources of error. We obtain closed-form expressions for the conventional and spin-dependent Josephson couplings. Despite their small probability, two-quasiparticle configurations, through coherence with the zero-quasiparticle component, supply exactly half of the leading spin-dependent Josephson coupling even without Coulomb repulsion and dominate it as the repulsion grows. Spin-orbit-induced spin transfer between the dot and the leads produces a Josephson-current contribution that is common to both qubit states and finite at zero phase bias when the dot and lead Zeeman energies differ. We also map the localization of the virtual quasiparticles and the spin density in the leads. The results connect strongly correlated quantum-dot models to effective Hamiltonians used for Andreev-spin-qubit circuits and clarify how the wavefunction structure determines their couplings.
summary: This work presents a quasiparticle-resolved variational theory for Andreev spin qubits, treating the system as a quantum dot coupled to superconducting leads. By retaining up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles, the authors derive analytical expressions for Josephson couplings, demonstrating the crucial role of virtual excitations in determining qubit behavior. This connects complex strongly correlated physics to practical circuit modeling.
main_problem: The paper develops a quasiparticle-resolved variational theory to accurately model the energy splittings and Josephson couplings in Andreev spin qubits (ASQs).
main_result: The theory shows that two-quasiparticle configurations significantly contribute to the spin-dependent Josephson coupling, and it provides closed-form expressions connecting correlated dot models to effective circuit Hamiltonians.
method: A continuum variational approach is employed, retaining configurations up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles, and results are benchmarked against NRG/DMRG calculations.
model_or_system: The system is an Andreev spin qubit realized in a quantum-dot Josephson junction, modeled by coupling an Anderson Impurity Model (AIM) to superconducting leads described by the BCS Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Josephson energies ($E_J, E_S$), quasiparticle composition, and site-resolved density matrices ($\varrho_s$).
important_parameters: Coulomb interaction ($U$), superconducting gap ($\Delta$), detuning ($\delta$), and superconducting phase difference ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The theory focuses on the odd-parity sector and utilizes variational approximations by truncating the QP configuration space to two quasiparticles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the microscopic model, the QP-sector hierarchy, and show convergence checks for observables like empty-dot probability and linear spin response against DMRG/NRG results.
paper_structure: The paper moves from defining the microscopic Hamiltonian (AIM coupled to BCS leads) to developing the variational ansatz, solving the resulting coupled integral equations in the continuum limit, and finally calculating specific observables like energy splittings and density matrices.
why_interesting: It provides a highly detailed, analytically tractable framework for understanding superconducting quantum circuits by explicitly resolving the role of virtual quasiparticle excitations in determining macroscopic couplings.
